transcript.text: my belling cooker keeps burnin stuff 1 day then next day its undercookd on same temp. been like it a cuple months. thermastat??

That fluctuating temperature is exactly what you’d expect from a failing thermostat or temperature sensor trying to regulate the heat. It could also be the control board getting confused, but the regulating component itself is the most common suspect here. To help narrow it down, please switch off and unplug the cooker for safety first. Then check if your model has a mechanical dial or an electronic display, as this tells us whether we are looking at a physical thermostat or an electronic sensor.
ok its got mechanical knobs and a little orange neon light, no display or anything. unplugged it too, its a belling 60cm double oven if that helps

With mechanical knobs, the most likely cause is a failing oven thermostat where the internal capillary isn't reading the temperature correctly. It could also be the fan motor struggling to circulate heat evenly, or just the cooling fan on the back not working properly. Since you have already unplugged it safely, please check if there are any obvious signs of damage to the wiring near the element or thermostat. Also, make sure you aren't using a "fast heat" or "booster" setting by mistake, as these can cause uneven cooking.

not sure how id check the wiring, i havnt got any tools and dont fancy taking the back off. i dont know what a fast heat or booster setting is, i just turn the knob to 180 like for my sponge recipes. what should i do next?

To help us figure out if it is just a setting issue or a part failure, please try baking something simple like a cake at 180°C and watch how it behaves. If it burns quickly even on that low setting, the thermostat is likely stuck "on" and not regulating the heat properly. If it takes ages to cook or stays undercooked despite the neon light being on, the heating element might be failing or the fan isn't circulating the air correctly. Please let me know how the food cooks during this test so we can decide if a repair engineer is needed.

ive already seen that tho, its burnt cakes some days and other days the lasagne is still cold in the middle, its random. do i really need to bake another cake to test it? the neon sometimes goes off after about 10 mins and sometimes stays on for ages if that helps

You don't need to bake another cake right now since you have already confirmed it is running hot and cold on the same setting. The fact that the neon light sometimes goes off after 10 minutes suggests the thermostat is trying to cycle, but it could be failing to regulate properly or the fan isn't circulating heat consistently. To help us narrow this down without taking anything apart, please check if your oven has a fan function symbol (a circle with a fan inside) and ensure you are using that for your sponge recipes. Also, let me know if the neon light stays on constantly when you first turn it on or if it flickers off almost immediately.

its a fan oven i think, i can hear the fan going when its on. not sure about the symbol on the knob tho. the neon doesnt flicker, it just stays on and then sometimes goes off after about 10 mins and other times it stays on for ages. like i said its random

That random behaviour with the neon light suggests the thermostat is struggling to keep the temperature steady or the fan isn't circulating heat evenly. Since you can hear the fan running, it might be worth checking if there is a specific "fan oven" symbol on your knob rather than just a standard heating symbol. Please also ensure that you are not accidentally selecting a different function like grill or base heat, which would explain why some days it burns and others it undercooks. If you can confirm the exact setting you use for your sponge recipes, we can better determine if the issue is with the thermostat or the control selector.
i just turn the main oven knob to 180, thats all i do, i dont touch any other setting. not sure what the symbols mean tbh. is it the thermostat then or do i need an engineer?

It is very likely the thermostat or temperature sensor, but it could also be the function selector switch getting confused about which setting you have chosen. Since you are unsure of the symbols and only use one knob, a faulty selector could be causing those random hot and cold cycles. To help us narrow this down without opening anything up, please check if your oven has a specific "fan" symbol (a circle with a fan inside) on the main knob. If it does, try using that setting specifically for your sponge recipes to see if the results are more consistent than when you use a different function.
